New Home Setup Checklist

The first days in a new home are the time to get the fundamentals right — where the shut-offs are, whether the alarms work, and getting the place clean before furniture fills it. This checklist covers the safety, admin, and settling-in tasks so your new place feels like home fast. More in our moving and home checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

New Home Setup Checklist · 18 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Locate and label the fuse box, water stopcock, and gas shut-off

    You'll want these in an emergency, not during one.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Test smoke and carbon-monoxide alarms and replace any dead batteries
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Take meter readings (gas, electric, water) and send them to your providers
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Confirm utilities, heating, and hot water all work
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Change the locks, or at least have the keys re-keyed

    You don't know who else still has a copy.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Set up and test your internet and Wi-Fi
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Do a deep clean before furniture arrives

    Kitchen, bathroom, and floors are easiest empty.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Check for leaks, damp, or pest signs and photograph any issues for your records
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Find the nearest hospital, pharmacy, and grocery store
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Learn your bin and recycling collection days and where the bins go
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Unpack your essentials box first: bedding, toiletries, chargers, and a kettle
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Register with a local doctor and dentist
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Introduce yourself to the neighbours and ask about parking and building quirks
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Update your address on IDs, accounts, and deliveries

    See the change-of-address checklist.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Set up a basic first-aid kit and a fire extinguisher
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Note your landlord's or property manager's emergency contact
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Program the thermostat and check every window and door lock
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Plan your furniture layout before hauling heavy items around

Frequently asked questions

What should I do first in a new home? expand_more

Before unpacking, find the fuse box, water stopcock, and gas shut-off, test the smoke and carbon-monoxide alarms, take meter readings, and confirm the utilities and heating work. Then change the locks and do a deep clean while the rooms are still empty.

Should I change the locks when I move in? expand_more

Yes — you have no way of knowing who still holds a copy of the old keys (previous tenants, agents, cleaners). Re-keying or replacing the locks is a cheap, one-time job that's well worth the peace of mind. Check your lease first if you're renting.

How do I set up utilities in a new home? expand_more

Contact each provider (electricity, gas, water, internet) a couple of weeks before moving to transfer or open accounts for your move date, then take meter readings on day one and send them in so you're only billed for what you use.
